faceBox.$comment: The ascent and descent a browser reports for a face. Every real font sets hhea and usWin to the same numbers, so only a font built to disagree can say which was read; and every probe on a 1000 em lands on a whole pixel, so only one that does not can say how the browser rounds it.
faceBox.answer: usWin, or sTypo when fsSelection bit 7 is set

kerning.$comment: A font may carry pair adjustments in a legacy kern table, in GPOS, or in both. The third probe sets them to different values, which is the only way to find out which one loses, and the fourth reaches its PairPos through a type 9 Extension lookup, which is how a font compiler emits one and where a reader that skips the type silently loses all kerning.
kerning.answer: GPOS when it yields a pair, else the kern table, following one type 9 Extension lookup

width.$comment: Whether an advance is linear in size - that is, unhinted - and how the browser quantises it. The linear reading is what matters on a slide; the quantisation is what lets the reader's test assert equality instead of a tolerance.
width.answer: advance truncated, kern rounded, both at 1/65536 px

ideographic.$comment: Where an upright East Asian glyph puts its baseline. A BASE table names a coordinate per script per baseline tag, so the reading has to say which tag, which script, and what a font without one falls back to; three fonts disagree with themselves on all three.
ideographic.answer: the BASE ideo coordinate of the DFLT script, else the face box descent, rounded as the box is
